claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses into every SqlBinaryExpression operator including AndAlso/OrElse (and Coalesce), which do not propagate NULL under three-valued logic; so for CASE WHEN a IS NOT NULL THEN (a AND b) ELSE NULL END the guard is dropped by DropNotNullChecks and the CASE collapses to a AND b, yielding FALSE/TRUE where NULL was expected. Reached via the ordinary null-semantics rewrite (a == b -> a = b AND b IS NOT NULL), so x.Nullable != null ? x.Nullable == x.Other : (bool?)null is miscompiled, giving wrong projected values and wrong row sets; the mirror-image transform at :2314-2321 already excludes AndAlso/OrElse. Fix should be an allow-list of genuinely null-propagating operators.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` treats `AndAlso`/`OrElse` operands as null-propagating, so `IS NOT NULL` guards are dropped from CASE expressions that do not actually propagate NULL — silently wrong query results

claim: Returning clause.Result instead of the CaseExpression could change the expression's Type/TypeMapping. Tool checked and marked [false]: CaseExpression derives both from whenClauses[0].Result so they are identical.

func.Instance! is dereferenced when InstancePropagatesNullability is true alone, whereas the sibling code at :2394 also requires Instance not null; the internal SqlFunctionExpression constructor permits that combination, though the worst case is a stray null in the HashSet with no observable effect. Tagged [minor] style inconsistency.

claim: NullPropagatedOperands walks the entire result subtree and inserts each node into a HashSet<SqlExpression> whose GetHashCode is structural and recursive, giving super-linear hashing on large result trees; runs only in the compile-once path when the pattern matches. Tagged [minor] micro-optimization.

claim: The HashSet<SqlExpression> of null-propagated operands might rely on reference equality and thus fail to match structurally-equal expressions. Tool checked and marked [false]: ColumnExpression, SqlBinaryExpression and SqlUnaryExpression override Equals/GetHashCode structurally; any type that does not would only cause a missed optimization.
